title: GTA 6 Release Date: Take-Two Says It Is Not for Sale
description: The GTA 6 release date is November 19, and Take-Two's CEO says the company won't sell itself after EA's $55 billion private buyout, per GameSpot.

body.text: With the GTA 6 release date set for November 19, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick says his company is not looking to be bought, according to GameSpot. The comments follow Electronic Arts going private in a $55 billion deal, and they matter because they signal that the publisher behind Grand Theft Auto plans to stay independent just as its biggest launch arrives.
What Zelnick said about Take-Two staying independent
GameSpot reports that EA was recently acquired by an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. That raised an obvious question: is Take-Two next?

Zelnick, speaking with David Rubenstein, said the results speak for themselves. In his view, Take-Two has shown it can thrive on its own, and it does not need a bigger parent to stay competitive. He also described the company's finances as strong.

His argument is about size. Zelnick said smaller companies, those earning under a billion in yearly revenue, can struggle to build, market and distribute games at scale. They may also find it harder to absorb a flop, which is part of the creative business.
Past that billion mark, he said, extra scale stops helping much. Take-Two's guidance for this fiscal year is $8 billion to $8.2 billion, according to GameSpot.
Take-Two has turned down suitors before

This is not the first time the question has come up. GameSpot notes that in early 2008, EA privately tried to buy Take-Two. The GTA and BioShock publisher rejected the approach, and EA then went public with its pursuit. Later that year EA dropped the plan after Take-Two said it was worth more and EA would not raise its bid.
In 2019, there were rumours that Sony wanted to buy Take-Two. GameSpot says that was ultimately treated as unconfirmed market chatter rather than a formal bid.
Take-Two's market cap is above $42 billion, and GameSpot says it is expected to grow in the year ahead. Any buyer would need a very large cheque.
The timing is hard to ignore. GTA 6 arrives on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and preloading is live now. That helps, since GameSpot says the game has a massive file size.
Zelnick has also hinted that future GTA games could arrive faster than the long gaps fans are used to. According to GameSpot, that could be good for Take-Two's financials.

items: How GTA 6 performs after its November 19 launch, and how that shapes Take-Two's revenue against its $8 billion to $8.2 billion guidance.
Whether any new details emerge on shorter gaps between GTA releases.
Whether more big publishers follow EA into private ownership, though Zelnick's stance suggests Take-Two will not.

body.text: For Indian players, the near-term story is simpler: download the game, clear the storage space and get ready for launch day. The ownership question looks settled for now, at least from Take-Two's side.

faqs.q: What is the GTA 6 release date?
faqs.a: According to GameSpot, GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is already available.

faqs.q: Is Take-Two being acquired after EA went private?
faqs.a: No. GameSpot reports that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company can do very well independently and does not need to join a larger organization to compete.

faqs.q: How much was EA sold for?
faqs.a: GameSpot reports that Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund.
